rationale: Author-of-record round 5 (confirm) on fix commit 0f7f2216 (worktree byte-identical at the reviewed commit; go build clean; full internal/hook suite green; all four new tests PASS individually including the crossed no-session/claimed-bead-session matrix; cmd/mindspec and internal/instruct -short both green). Both round-4 convergent asks are delivered correctly and scoped exactly to the round-3-touched file pair plus their test file. G1 (ambiguity nil-route): the diagnosis is exact and consistent with the code I have read across all five rounds — derive.go's WorktreeMain switch genuinely has no `err == nil && len(specs) > 1` case (the deliberate 'caller handles ambiguity' fall-through leaves Phase empty with DerivationFailed FALSE), so round-3's DerivationFailed-only sentinel left a second post-initialization door to the narrowed nil check. The fix unifies ReadState's predicate with cmd/mindspec/instruct_tail.go:30's identical `ctx.DerivationFailed || ctx.Phase == ""` for the same Context shape — closing precisely the intra-bead contract-divergence class this bead exists to eliminate — renames the latch to `indeterminate` (it now covers two shapes), and HONESTLY rewrites the round-3 invariant comment whose 'only WorktreeMain's error arm reaches here' claim round-4's probe falsified (the same retract-inaccurate-claims discipline rounds 3 and 4 established). The supporting invariant — WorktreeSpec/WorktreeBead never produce an empty Phase thanks to round-1's unconditional backfills, so every empty-Phase Context reaching the latch is post-initialization — matches derive.go as landed. Nil is now unreachable post-init by construction, with the !indeterminate gate kept as declared belt-and-suspenders. G2 (indeterminate fail-closed on spec branches): the fall-through was real — ModeIndeterminate matched neither the idle fast-path (dispatch.go:108) nor the implement literal (:150) and reached the final Pass. The new check (:125) sits ahead of the implement literal, Blocks with an honest message naming the actual cause (discovery failure or ambiguity — never claiming the mode is implement), termsafe-escapes the branch, offers doctor + the worktree redirect, and preserves the MINDSPEC_ALLOW_MAIN=1 escape hatch. Scope note verified deliberately: an indeterminate mode on a non-spec, non-protected branch (e.g. bead/*) still passes — the designed permissive default for bead-branch commits and exactly the tally's stated scope (spec branches), not an oversight. The commit's consumer-check claim ('exactly one other Mode reader, no second Mode-literal switch') verified by grep: Mode is read only at dispatch.go:93 (protected-branch block, any mode — an indeterminate mode renders honestly in that message too), :108, :125, and :150; the only external consumer is cmd/mindspec/hook.go:74 passing ReadState into Run. Tests pin all the right things: the two G1 tests reproduce the exact bypass fixture (two healthy active specs, no session -> non-nil ModeIndeterminate; real Run("pre-commit") -> Block), and TestPreCommit_SpecBranch_IndeterminateFailsClosed drives a real WorktreeSpec-shaped fixture crossed over both session variants, with the healthy_implement_blocks legs confirming the pre-existing spec-branch implement block is undisturbed and the discovery_failure legs proving session metadata can never mask the sentinel. My round-4 defensive note (ReadState's reliance on ResolveContext's always-nil error contract) remains open as a non-blocking future-proofing nit — unchanged this round and still unreachable today. Incidental corroboration: internal/instruct's short suite completed in 39.8s this round now that panel test concurrency has subsided, supporting round-4's contention disposition of the 10m timeout. Verdict: APPROVE.

findings.title: Round-4 G1 confirmed: ambiguity nil-route closed by unifying ReadState's predicate with instruct_tail.go's, nil unreachable post-init by construction
findings.detail: The WorktreeMain multi-active-spec arm's deliberate empty-Phase fall-through (DerivationFailed false) was a second door past round-3's DerivationFailed-only latch; the widened `ctx.DerivationFailed || ctx.Phase == ""` predicate now matches instruct_tail.go:30 exactly for the same Context shape, and the round-3 comment whose 'only the error arm reaches here' claim was falsified is honestly rewritten to name both shapes. WorktreeSpec/WorktreeBead's round-1 unconditional backfills guarantee no third empty-Phase shape exists — verified against derive.go as landed. Both new G1 tests reproduce the bypass and PASS.

findings.title: Round-4 G2 confirmed: spec-branch indeterminate fail-closed with an honest message; permissive bead-branch default deliberately preserved
findings.detail: The new dispatch.go check Blocks ModeIndeterminate on spec/* ahead of the implement-literal check, naming the real cause rather than claiming implement mode, with termsafe branch escaping and the existing escape hatch. The Mode-reader inventory claim verified by grep (four dispatch sites, one external ReadState consumer). Indeterminate on non-spec, non-protected branches still passes — in-scope by the tally's own framing and consistent with the bead-branch workflow. The crossed test matrix pins both the new fail-closed legs and the undisturbed healthy-implement block, with session metadata proven unable to mask the sentinel.

findings.title: Carried non-blocking nit: ResolveContext always-nil error contract
findings.detail: My round-4 observation stands unchanged: ReadState's `ctxErr == nil && ctx != nil` guard would leave hs empty with indeterminate=false if phase.ResolveContext ever gained an error-returning path (none exists today — verified at round 4 against derive.go's single `return ctx, nil`). Treating ctxErr!=nil/ctx==nil as indeterminate would make the invariant self-contained; suitable as a post-spec follow-up, not a change request. Also for the audit trail: internal/instruct's short suite ran 39.8s this round under normal load, corroborating round-4's classification of the 10m package timeout as panel-concurrency contention.
